title: observability: add token-level KV cache metrics + tracing enrichment, dashboards and alert tuning
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: surface token-level KV cache metrics and enrich tracing spans so teams can correlate cache behavior with per-token latency and cost. This PR adds new Prometheus metrics for KV cache hits/misses/bypass rates at token granularity, enriches runtime tracing with KV cache annotations, updates Grafana dashboards for token-level cost/latency breakdowns, and tunes alert thresholds to reduce noisy pages.

What changed: checklist:
- [x] Export token-level KV cache metrics (kv_token_hits_total, kv_token_misses_total, kv_token_bypass_total, kv_token_evictions_total) with labels {model, shard, route, tenant}
- [x] Add derived PromQL rules for token-level cost-per-token and 95th/99th latency percentiles
- [x] Enrich tracing spans with kv.cache.hit and kv.cache.latency attributes; add span link reference when a remote fallback occurs
- [x] Create Grafana dashboard (observability/dashboards/token_kv_cost_latency.json) with per-model and per-route breakdowns and quick filters for tenant and shard
- [x] Add/adjust alerting rules: reduce false positives by using rolling-window aggregations and increase severity only when sustained regression observed
- [x] Docs: observability/kv_metrics.md with instrumentation notes and recommended runbooks
- [x] Unit + integration tests for metric naming and basic histogram buckets

Notes on approach: We opted for token-level counters (monotonic) with dimension labels to avoid cardinality explosion; dashboards use rollups and histogram aggregations to present per-token averages efficiently. Tracing enrichment is gated behind config flag env REDWOOD_KV_OBSERVABILITY=true to allow staged enablement in Dedicated/Private.

Related work: builds on ENG-3254 (token-level observability RFC) and ENG-3278 (kv cache metrics prototype). Addresses monitoring gaps surfaced during recent incident INT-2025 where a silent KV miss storm increased p99 latency for text-generation routes.

Testing and rollout: added unit tests and a small end-to-end job in perf-canary that exercises kv cache hit/miss patterns. Rollout will be staged: enable flag in dev, canary in prod-noncritical region, then global. Alert changes will be pushed to a new alerting folder observability/alerts/kv-adjusted-alerts.yaml to allow rollback without touching existing rules.

Backward compatibility: metric names are additive; no existing metrics removed. Tracing attributes are additive and behind a flag.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Nice work — can you justify choosing token-level counters vs. a sampled histogram for cost? Concerned about label explosion for tenants.

Ava Chen: We keep labels limited to {model, shard, route, tenant} and rely on rollups in PromQL and dashboard filters. Explicitly avoided high-cardinality runtime labels like prompt_hash. Added note in docs explaining tradeoffs.
Priya Nair: Alert thresholds look better but can we use a 15m sustained window before paging? Current change uses 5m; requests dir change.
Ava Chen: Updated alerts to use 15m sustained window and added a secondary 'warning' severity at 5m in the new alerts file. See observability/alerts/kv-adjusted-alerts.yaml.
Santiago Ruiz: Unit tests are flakey on CI (test_kv_histogram occasionally times out). Could be environment sensitive; please add a retry or increase timeout.
Ava Chen: Increased test timeout and added deterministic seed for histogram sampling. Reran CI.
Diego Morales: Approving after changes — left minor nit about dashboard panel titles (optional).
Priya Nair: Approved — good to merge once CI is green and canary runs complete.
release_notes: Add token-level KV cache metrics, tracing enrichment, Grafana dashboard for token-level cost/latency, and tuned alerting to reduce noise. Backwards compatible (additive metrics/attributes).
notes_for_ops: Enable via REDWOOD_KV_OBSERVABILITY=true. Rollout: dev -> canary (perf-canary/kv_observability_smoke) -> prod. If noisy alerts observed, rollback by reverting observability/alerts/kv-adjusted-alerts.yaml to previous alert set.
